gaps.description: Nothing blocks a direct /gabe-execute (or any source Write) while the phase's Red cell is ⬜ — 'before execute's first source Write' is enforced only when the operator happens to route through /gabe-next; no PreToolUse hook checks Red state on source edits.

gaps.description: plan-proof-guard verifies only record EXISTENCE and CITED-sha reachability — red-spec line 85 states plainly 'a record citing no sha passes'; a fabricated Cases: line with no red@sha ticks Red ✅ unblocked.
gaps.consequence: Record-shaped lies pass the D7 hook; only the prose gate and later review can distinguish them.

gaps.description: The red failure is never machine-re-verified after mint time: the tautology check is declared perishable, prove-guard.py re-runs are 'when the claim matters' with no trigger, cadence, or routing beat pointing at it.
gaps.consequence: Void guards (twin-measured 1-in-6) render as protection until the day they miss a real regression.

gaps.description: Spec/hook severity drift: red-spec says the commit-gate 'requires an id at birth' for new test files and calls the corpus check 'the enforcement hook', but both pre-checkpoint.sh checks are [WARN]-only echoes that never block.
gaps.consequence: Id-less test files and phantom declared C-ids commit cleanly despite the spec's 'requires' wording.

gaps.description: The RED: carve-out's hard logic — every declared id fails BY ASSERTION, nothing outside the set fails, import errors block — exists only as gate-spec prose; gabe-commit/scripts contains no script implementing the partition.
gaps.consequence: A sloppy gate run can bless a NOT-RED (import/collection-error) checkpoint as evidence.

gaps.description: Execute's phase-completion condition ('every declared case green AND every guard still green') and the case-scoped tests: line are both prose rules; no script cross-checks the verify run's ids against the phase's cases record.
gaps.consequence: Exec can tick ✅ with a declared case never turned green if narration slips.

gaps.description: Squash-merge protection for the red commit is a printed warning only; unreachable shas are caught only for shas actually CITED, only on the next PLAN write — guard-only records cite none, and nothing detects a squash after the plan archives.
gaps.consequence: Ever-red addresses silently go dark; 'has this case ever been observed failing' becomes unanswerable.

gaps.description: /gabe-execute itself has NO Red precondition: Step 0 validates .kdbp, active plan, Exec column, and project type, but never reads the Red column. Red-before-exec ordering lives solely in the /gabe-next router (next.mjs line 113), so a direct `/gabe-execute` invocation bypasses the only enforcement.
gaps.consequence: Invoking /gabe-execute directly on a Red ⬜ phase implements code test-last with zero warning.

gaps.description: The TASK CONTRACT fallback 'none declared (no /gabe-red record)' is self-certified: execute never distinguishes an enumerated skip code (skip:guard-only, skip:no-runtime-surface, skip:migration, skip:spike, skip:blocked-external — defined only in red-spec.md lines 111-116) from a red that simply never ran, and never surfaces or validates which skip applied.
gaps.consequence: A never-ran red reads identically to a legitimate enumerated skip; the omission is invisible until review.

gaps.description: 'Every declared case is green AND every guard is still green' before phase finish (execute-spec line 176) is prose-only. Step 7's deterministic invariants check journey-proof artifacts via `ls` and the Commit column, but nothing re-runs or re-checks the declared C-ids before Exec ticks ✅, and the plan-proof-guard hook checks only proof-path existence and red@sha reachability.
gaps.consequence: Exec can tick ✅ with declared cases still red if the model forgets the prose rule.

gaps.description: The case-scoped `tests:` evidence line (execute-spec line 207) has no validator: nothing checks that the `-k` expression actually covers every declared C-id and guard from the Cases: record, only that some case-scoped command ran and its count was copied.
gaps.consequence: A partial -k expression missing one declared id passes as full green.

gaps.description: The router's resume rule outranks red: `c.exec === "in_progress"` matches before the red check (next.mjs lines 112-113, 'never retro-blocked' by design). Once Exec is 🔄 — including via a direct /gabe-execute start that skipped red — /gabe-next routes back to execute for that phase.
gaps.consequence: One direct execute start permanently sidelines red from routing for that phase.

gaps.description: plan-proof-guard has no cross-cell ordering predicate: it blocks Red ✅ without a cases record, but Red ⬜ (or absent) combined with Exec ✅ passes the hook clean — the hook enforces record honesty, not the red-before-exec sequence.

gaps.description: Red is opt-in at two layers with warn-only debt: projects without a Red column are never routed to red (next.mjs lines 95-96), and prior phases with Red ⬜ only produce a printed warning while routing continues (lines 71, 83-84).
gaps.consequence: Skipped red on earlier phases accrues as a scrollable warning, never a stop.

gaps.description: Review never verifies red→green: no step runs, greps, or reads pass state for the phase's declared Cases ids — Step 3.4 only mints/bumps/drift-judges triage subjects; Coverage is diff-shaped and Runtime Evidence (Step 3.2) checks PLAN.json proof entries, not C-ids.

gaps.description: No declared-vs-corpus reconciliation at review time: NEW CASE fires only from diff branch analysis; a /gabe-red id whose test was never written or was deleted is invisible to review — the only existence check is pre-checkpoint's commit-time grep, a WARN that gates nothing.
gaps.consequence: A declared id with zero corpus hits passes review; only a dismissible commit warning remains downstream.

gaps.description: CASE DRIFT is judgment-only by design (D6) with no deterministic backstop in review or the hook — pre-checkpoint greps id tokens, never assertion strength.
gaps.consequence: A weakened assertion under an unchanged id ships; the center keeps citing the case as guarding.

gaps.description: Step 3.4 activation lacks a deterministic detection step (contrast Step 0.3's zero-LLM PLAN parse): nothing in the procedure forces reading Phase Details cases records or the center's angle verdicts before scoring dimensions.
gaps.consequence: On a red-beat project the entire case-estate layer can silently skip, producing a plain review.

gaps.description: Reserved C[next] allocation (corpus max(grep)+1) has no collision handling — unlike Sub-check 5b's documented D[N] race retry — and a reserved id is uncommitted until a triage fix/defer lands it.
gaps.consequence: Concurrent review and red runs can mint duplicate C-ids, corrupting the center and hook joins.

gaps.description: GROWTH subjects beyond the cap of 7 per review are neither priced nor persisted by review; they exist only as the center's list.
gaps.consequence: Low-ranked angles may stay on hand-authored fallback verdicts indefinitely, never entering triage.

gaps.description: Case outcomes leave no audit trace: the LEDGER row schema and the Review-tick pass condition carry no case fields (no green counts, no NEW CASE/BUMP/DRIFT tallies), and PENDING rows only capture deferrals.
gaps.consequence: Nothing downstream can distinguish 'cases verified green' from 'cases never examined' for a ticked phase.

gaps.description: Review ✅ has NO evidence check anywhere: plan-proof-guard validates only cells.red and cells.exec; no hook, script, or fixture verifies a review ran, findings were triaged, or cases pass before Review flips to done.
gaps.consequence: A Review ✅ can be flipped as a lie; the router then deterministically routes /gabe-commit on unreviewed code.

gaps.description: Exec ✅ with `proof: null` passes plan-proof-guard (fixture run.sh:54 pins this). Nothing deterministic forces a proof to be DECLARED; gabe-plan's proof_type declaration and gabe-execute's proof-writing are prose, and evidence-freshness.sh only WARNs.
gaps.consequence: A phase can close Exec ✅ with zero evidence simply by never declaring a proof line.

gaps.description: The red@<sha> check verifies only that the commit EXISTS (git cat-file -e); it never inspects the commit for failing tests matching the declared C-ids, and a cases record citing no sha at all passes (fixture run.sh:60).
gaps.consequence: Any reachable sha — even an unrelated commit — satisfies Red ✅; assertion-red proof is prose in gabe-red's spec.

gaps.description: The red→execute ordering binds only when work is dispatched through /gabe-next. next.mjs is READ-ONLY ('prints the decision'); no hook blocks invoking /gabe-execute directly or editing source files while Red is ⬜, and exec in_progress resumes without ever being retro-red-gated.
gaps.consequence: TDD ordering is skippable by not asking the router; only the PLAN-cell lie is caught later.

gaps.description: The entire gabe-commit gate (CHECK 1–9, severity table, RED carve-out, force-commit ledger row) is prose executed by the model; the only deterministic guard on raw `git commit` is pre-checkpoint.sh, which by design 'never blocks — debts warn'.
gaps.consequence: One raw git commit bypasses every commit check with only a [WARN] line as friction.

gaps.description: The RED-trailer carve-out has no script: no deterministic parser extracts the RED: trailer, reruns the declared C-ids, or distinguishes assertion-failure from import/collection error — the spec instructs the model to verify this.
gaps.consequence: A fake red (collection error, or passing tests mislabeled) can be committed as a red checkpoint if the model mis-verifies.

gaps.description: plan-proof-guard is a PostToolUse hook on Write|Edit targeting *.kdbp/PLAN.json|PLAN.md paths; PLAN edits via Bash (sed/jq/python), git operations, or merges never trigger it, and a missing python3 makes it INERT with exit 0 (fail-open, line 28).
gaps.consequence: The lie-block is bypassable via any shell-side PLAN edit; on a python3-less host it silently stops guarding.

gaps.description: No mechanism ever checks that declared cases PASS (green): pre-checkpoint greps only for the id's textual existence in the corpus; nothing runs the C-id tests before Exec ✅, Review ✅, or Push. gabe-execute's 'case-scoped verify' and gabe-push's production gates are prose.
